title: Self-Gravitation of Mode Quanta in a Causal Resonator: One-Loop Finiteness in Linearized Quantum Gravity and the Emergence of the Dark-Energy Scale
abstract: Perturbative quantum gravity is ultraviolet divergent and, as shown by 't Hooft and Veltman, non-renormalizable. A recent object-relative, Lorentz-invariant weighting of internal electromagnetic modes renders selected one-loop contributions of quantum electrodynamics finite without counterterms. Here that weighting is derived rather than postulated: causality defines a mode resonator bounded by the Hubble radius and re-defined in every inertial frame, and the self-gravitation of each mode quantum deforms its spectrum. Applied to linearized gravity, the graviton self-coupling reaches order unity at the Planck wave number, so that the mode content available to a loop is suppressed beyond it. Any suppression exceeding a threshold fixed by the diagram renders the one-loop integrals finite; no cutoff is imposed and no mode structure above the Planck scale need be derived. For pure gravity the same power counting extends to every loop order, and the leading suppression already meets the resulting condition for every topology with more than one vertex; a single class of single-vertex insertions is excluded. The Bianchi identity takes the role of the Ward identity at one loop, and the transformation between the resonators of two inertial frames is unitary. The same finite mode content yields a vacuum energy density of order H^2/G, of the observed sign and magnitude, from the Planck and causal infrared wave numbers alone. A contribution tracking the instantaneous expansion rate is an exact rescaling of the gravitational constant and is excluded by primordial nucleosynthesis, so the mode basis must be frozen in any inertial system; referring it to the stationary de Sitter horizon fixes the remaining coefficient to the geometric value 6/pi and makes a value for the energy density of gravitational vacuum fluctuations possible which can be interpreted as origin of the dark-energy effect.
summary: This theoretical work tackles the divergence problem in quantum gravity by proposing that causality defines a 'causal resonator' that naturally regularizes quantum loop calculations. By applying a derived mode weighting, the authors show that the resulting finite mode content yields a vacuum energy density matching the observed dark energy scale, offering a potential resolution to the cosmological constant problem.
main_problem: The paper addresses the ultraviolet divergence and non-renormalizability of perturbative quantum gravity while simultaneously aiming to derive the observed dark-energy scale from fundamental principles.
main_result: The introduction of a causality-derived, object-relative mode weighting renders one-loop quantum gravity integrals finite, naturally yielding a vacuum energy density proportional to $H_0^2/G$ with the correct sign and magnitude.
method: The authors employ a novel mode-relative weighting technique applied to loop calculations in linearized quantum gravity, constrained by a 'causal resonator' defined by the Hubble radius.
model_or_system:
The model is linearized quantum gravity, treating the gravitational field as a perturbation $h_{\mu
u}$ around flat spacetime. The key physical constraint is the causal boundary defined by the Hubble radius, which dictates the available mode spectrum.
key_observables: Vacuum energy density ($ho_{vac}$), which is predicted to be $\sim H_0^2/G$, and the convergence of one-loop integrals.
important_parameters: The Hubble radius ($R_H$), the Planck length ($l_P$), and the resulting characteristic scales $	ilde{k}_{IR} = H_0/(4c)$ and $\kappa_P = 1/l_P$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions include that physical mode spectra are constrained by causal coherence, that gravitational self-backreaction deforms the mode spectrum, and that the causal boundary is consistently defined across all inertial frames.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the divergence problem in quantum gravity, then introducing the causal resonator and the associated mode weighting derived from causality. It applies this weighting to calculate one-loop corrections, demonstrating finiteness, and finally uses the resulting finite mode content to calculate the vacuum energy density, linking it to the dark energy scale.
why_interesting: While focused on gravity, the concept of deriving a physical constraint (causality) to regularize a divergent quantum field theory calculation is conceptually related to finding natural cutoffs or constraints in many-body systems, though the specific mathematical tools are distinct.
